walnuts.name: Walnuts
walnuts.description: Walnuts are a unique superfood rich in alpha-linolenic acid (Omega-3) and antioxidants. They are renowned for supporting brain health and cardiovascular function due to their high nutrient density.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: High-energy food; recommended for consumption in moderate portions.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: A good source of plant-based protein.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Primarily healthy polyunsaturated fatty acids, including Omega-3s.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Includes dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

microNutrients.name: Omega-3 (ALA)
microNutrients.description: High content of alpha-linolenic acid, which supports heart health.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Essential for the nervous system and blood pressure regulation.

healthBenefits: Brain Support: High levels of antioxidants and Omega-3s improve cognitive function.
Heart Health: Helps lower levels of 'bad' LDL cholesterol.
Inflammation Control: Contains compounds that reduce chronic inflammatory processes.
precautions: Caloric Density: Due to the high caloric density, portion control is recommended.
Allergy: Nuts are a common and severe allergen for many individuals.
Oxidation: The oils in nuts oxidize quickly; store in a cool, dark place to maintain quality.

onions.name: Onions
onions.description: Onions are a versatile vegetable known for their high content of phytonutrients, particularly flavonoids and sulfur compounds. Beyond adding depth of flavor to culinary dishes, they possess significant anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that support metabolic health.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A low-calorie food rich in fiber and biologically active compounds.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains a small amount of plant-based protein.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Contains negligible amounts of fat.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Contains natural sugars and prebiotic dietary fibers that are beneficial for gut microflora.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: Supports immune function and helps protect cells from damage.

microNutrients.name: Quercetin
microNutrients.description: A potent flavonoid antioxidant that helps fight inflammation and supports heart health.

healthBenefits: Heart Health: Regular consumption helps improve blood circulation and maintain healthy cholesterol levels.
Antioxidant Support: A high concentration of quercetin helps neutralize free radicals.
Microbiome Support: The prebiotic fibers in onions serve as food for beneficial gut bacteria.
Anti-inflammatory Effects: Sulfur compounds assist in reducing inflammatory markers in the body.
precautions: Digestive Sensitivity: In some individuals, raw onions may cause bloating or heartburn.
Eye Irritation: Cutting onions releases volatile substances that can irritate the eyes.
Individual Intolerance: Allergic reactions to components of the plant are possible.

garlic.name: Garlic
garlic.description: Garlic is an aromatic plant of the onion family, renowned for its potent biologically active compounds. Due to its high content of sulfur-containing substances, such as allicin, it is not only an essential culinary spice but also a natural antiseptic with significant immunomodulatory properties.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A source of moderate energy. The primary value of garlic lies in its phytonutrients rather than its caloric density.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains plant-based protein rich in sulfur-containing amino acids necessary for metabolism.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Minimal fat content, making garlic a diet-friendly food.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Consists mainly of complex carbohydrates and fiber, which support gut health.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: A powerful antioxidant that supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: Essential for the metabolism of proteins and carbohydrates, as well as the functioning of enzymatic defense systems in the body.

microNutrients.name: Allicin
microNutrients.description: A key sulfur-containing compound formed when garlic is crushed; it possesses antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties.

healthBenefits: Immune System Support: Regular consumption helps reduce the frequency and severity of colds by enhancing the body's defensive functions.
Cardiovascular Support: Helps maintain normal blood pressure levels and contributes to lowering total cholesterol.
Antioxidant Protection: Its rich composition of sulfur compounds neutralizes free radicals, slowing down oxidative processes in cells.
Detoxification: Facilitates the removal of heavy metals and supports the natural cleansing processes of the liver.
precautions: Mucosal Irritation: In its raw form, garlic can be aggressive to the stomach lining and esophagus, especially for individuals with gastritis or peptic ulcer disease.
Blood Effects: It has a mild blood-thinning effect; those taking anticoagulants should consult with a physician.
Individual Intolerance: Allergic reactions or individual sensitivity may occur, manifesting as gastrointestinal discomfort.
Specific Odor: Volatile sulfur compounds can cause a persistent odor on the breath and skin, which is a byproduct of allicin metabolism.

avocados.name: Avocado
avocados.description: Avocado is an uniquely structural, lipid-dense fruit. Renowned for its rich concentration of monounsaturated oleic acid instead of natural sugars, it serves as an exceptional functional food to drive deep fat-soluble nutrient absorption, cardiovascular protection, and metabolic satiety.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Higher in energy than typical fruits, delivering dense, clean metabolic fuel derived from high-quality monounsaturated fats.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Provides nominal plant proteins containing essential building blocks to assist in daily cellular tissue maintenance.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: An exceptional matrix of heart-healthy fats, overwhelmingly dominated by oleic acid, which maximizes fat-soluble nutrient delivery.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Mainly composed of complex structural dietary fibers with practically zero simple sugars, yielding a near-flat glycemic curve.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A brilliant blend of soluble and insoluble fibers that supports digestive regularity, balances gut microbiota, and optimizes satiety.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An outstanding concentration—surpassing bananas—that regulates fluid pump mechanics, neural signaling, and resting vascular tone.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid)
microNutrients.description: A major catalytic factor required for cellular hormone synthesis, fatty acid oxidation, and optimizing daily cognitive pathways.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B9 (Folate)
microNutrients.description: Crucial for deep cellular division, DNA replication, and supporting the healthy synthesis of red blood cells.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin E
microNutrients.description: A premier lipid-soluble antioxidant that actively guards tissue membranes against oxidative deterioration and preserves skin health.

microNutrients.name: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
microNutrients.description: Targeted plant carotenoids that concentrate in the eye's macular area, absorbing harmful blue wave frequencies and protecting vision.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Optimization: Rich in monounsaturated fats (oleic acid) and plant sterols, avocado helps regulate low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol ratios and supports endothelial vascular health.

Unrivaled Nutrient Assimilation: Acts as an ideal lipid delivery vehicle. Adding avocado to raw vegetable meals can increase the biological absorption of companion fat-soluble antioxidants (like beta-carotene) up to fifteen-fold.
Advanced Potassium Performance: Supplying more potassium than a banana, it actively aids in lowering blood pressure levels, managing cellular fluid dynamics, and reducing sodium retention.
Sustained Metabolic Satiety: The dense combination of healthy fats and complex dietary fiber slows gastric emptying rates, keeping insulin curves incredibly flat and promoting long-lasting fullness.
precautions: High Caloric Accumulation: Due to its high lipid profile, avocado is significantly more energy-dense than other fruits. If strict caloric management or weight reduction is your primary goal, maintaining precise serving boundaries is recommended.

Latex-Fruit Syndrome Cross-Reactivity: Individuals possessing diagnosed allergies to natural rubber latex may experience mild to severe cross-reactive responses to avocados due to structurally similar plant defense proteins (chitinases).

FODMAP Fermentation Bloating: Avocado houses measurable levels of sorbitol, a natural sugar alcohol. Those with sensitive gastrointestinal tracts or functional Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) may notice mild abdominal gas or bloating if over-consuming.

Prescription Blood Thinner Synergy: Avocados carry moderate quantities of Vitamin K1, which coordinates blood-coagulation cascades. If you are taking highly calibrated prescription anticoagulants (like Warfarin), keeping your avocado intake relatively consistent is helpful.

beef-liver.name: Beef Liver
beef-liver.description: Beef liver is widely regarded as the ultimate king of superfoods. It contains an unmatched, highly concentrated matrix of pre-formed vitamins, essential minerals, and complete proteins, making it drastically superior to standard muscle meats in nutritional value.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Provides nutrient-dense energy with a very low caloric cost relative to its massive vitamin profile.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: An exceptionally rich source of highly bioavailable, complete protein containing all essential amino acids for tissue synthesis.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Low in total lipids, featuring a balanced profile of monounsaturated, polyunsaturated, and essential saturated fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Sourced naturally from stored animal glycogen. It represents a rare carbohydrate presence in meat, keeping a low glycemic index.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (Retinol)
microNutrients.description: Pre-formed active Vitamin A (retinol) that directly fuels the visual cycle, maintains endothelial integrity, and fortifies systemic immunity.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: An astronomical concentration essential for myelin sheath repair, DNA replication, and preventing megaloblastic anemia.

microNutrients.name: Copper
microNutrients.description: Acts as a vital biochemical catalyst for iron metabolism, collagen structure synthesis, and defense against oxidative stress.

microNutrients.name: Iron (Heme)
microNutrients.description: Highly absorbable heme iron that binds instantly to hemoglobin, optimizing cellular oxygen transport and preventing fatigue.

microNutrients.name: Folate (Vitamin B9)
microNutrients.description: Critical for cellular division, rapid amino acid conversion, and optimizing prenatal neural tube development.

microNutrients.name: Choline
microNutrients.description: A foundational building block for cell membrane phospholipids and the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, driving memory and cognitive focus.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
microNutrients.description: Crucial for mitochondrial respiration, electron transport chains, and converting macronutrients into actual ATP energy units.

healthBenefits: Unrivaled Anemia Prevention: The combination of high-density heme iron, copper, and vitamin B12 provides all necessary structural raw materials for efficient red blood cell production.
Advanced Cognitive Architecture: Tremendous concentrations of B-vitamins paired with Choline maximize neurotransmitter generation, preserving rapid brain signaling and nervous system integrity.
Enhanced Metabolic Performance: Acts as a powerful coenzyme powerhouse; its extreme riboflavin and pantothenic acid values catalyze the rapid breakdown of dietary elements into pure kinetic energy.

Immune & Vision Optimization: Provides massive doses of active, bioavailable retinol (Vitamin A) that directly strengthens cornea function, supports night vision, and reinforces white blood cell response.
precautions: Vitamin A Toxicity (Hypervitaminosis A): Because liver holds pre-formed Vitamin A, which is fat-soluble and stores in our tissues, eating it daily can cause toxicity. Limiting consumption to 1-2 times per week is highly advised.

Pregnancy Safety Thresholds: Expectant mothers should strictly manage liver intake. Excess pre-formed Vitamin A (retinol) carries a documented risk of causing congenital developmental defects in the fetus.

Copper Accumulation Risk: The extremely high copper content means frequent intake can over-accumulate in the body, which might lead to oxidative strain or complicate issues for individuals with underlying copper metabolic conditions.

Purine Density & Gout Management: Organ meats are naturally heavy in purine structures. These break down into uric acid, which can aggregate inside joints and trigger painful flares in individuals prone to gout.

bell-peppers.name: Bell Peppers
bell-peppers.description: Bell peppers are a remarkably crisp, refreshing, and nutrient-dense vegetable. Containing an unparalleled mega-dose of Vitamin C alongside a rich array of protective carotenoid antioxidants, they serve as an elite whole food for optimizing immune defense, skin elasticity, and vision.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Very low in calories and highly hydrating, making it an excellent volume food for blood sugar control and weight management.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains minor plant-based amino acids, serving as structural support within the vegetable's crisp cellular matrix.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Virtually fat-free. However, pairing bell peppers with healthy dietary lipids (like olive oil) drastically boosts fat-soluble carotenoid absorption.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Composed of natural simple sugars (glucose, fructose) wrapped in structured dietary fibers, ensuring a negligible glycemic response.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: An astronomical concentration that effortlessly beats citrus fruits, driving powerful collagen synthesis, tissue repair, and immune performance.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (Beta-Carotene)
microNutrients.description: Rich in provitamin A carotenoids, which the body converts to active retinol to preserve night vision and maintain healthy mucosal barriers.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
microNutrients.description: Acts as a vital metabolic coenzyme required for the proper synthesis of red blood cells and neuro-signaling transmitters.

microNutrients.name: Capsanthin
microNutrients.description: A powerful, unique antioxidant responsible for the bright red hue; it scavenges free radicals and assists in protecting cellular health.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An essential systemic electrolyte that coordinates electrical cardiac pulses, fluid pump mechanics, and balanced blood pressure levels.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: Provides crisp structural fibers that optimize transit time in the digestive tract and feed beneficial gut microbiomes.

healthBenefits: Unrivaled Immune System Defense: Delivering over 140% of your daily Vitamin C in just 100g, bell peppers rapidly stimulate white blood cell production and bolster host defense mechanisms.
Advanced Ocular Protection: Loaded with lutein, zeaxanthin, and beta-carotene, frequent intake helps shield the retina from high-energy light damage and counteracts age-related visual degeneration.
Dermal Integrity & Anti-Aging: The heavy synthesis of Vitamin C works in perfect synergy with Vitamin E to maximize natural collagen assembly, improving vascular tone and skin elasticity.
Enhanced Iron Bioavailability: The incredible concentration of ascorbic acid transforms non-heme iron from companion plant-based foods into highly soluble, easily absorbable forms inside the gut.
precautions: Nightshade Sensitive Profile: As prominent members of the nightshade family, bell peppers house trace alkaloids. While safe for the vast majority, individuals with specific autoimmune conditions or joint sensitivities may choose to track their tolerance.

Gastrointestinal Skin & Seed Irritation: The structural outer skin and internal seeds contain dense fibers that can sometimes be tough to process for sensitive stomachs, occasionally causing mild bloating or reflux unless peeled or cooked.

Pesticide Surface Retention: Because of their broad surface area and thin skins, conventionally farmed bell peppers can hold higher pesticide residues. Washing thoroughly or choosing organic options is beneficial.

Cross-Reactive Pollen Allergies: Individuals with specific seasonal allergies (such as birch or mugwort pollen) might experience mild cross-reactive oral allergy syndrome, presenting as itching in the mouth or throat.

broccoli.name: Broccoli
broccoli.description: Broccoli is an elite, highly complex cruciferous vegetable powerhouse. Packaging a monumental density of immune-boosting Vitamin C and bone-building Vitamin K1 alongside legendary cellular detox compounds like *sulforaphane*, it serves as a premier functional whole food for total body resilience and tissue defense.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Very low in calories and exceptionally nutrient-dense, making it a perfect functional volume food for strict metabolic and weight management.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains a surprisingly robust plant-based protein profile for a green vegetable, supplying clean essential amino acids for tissue repair.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Virtually fat-free. However, cooking or serving it with a splash of healthy lipids drastically increases the absorption of its fat-soluble vitamins.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Composed of slow-digesting complex carbohydrates tightly wrapped in rigid plant fiber structures, keeping blood sugar curves completely flat.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: An exceptional concentration that easily rival or beats most citrus fruits, fueling robust immune mechanics and dynamic collagen assembly.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K1 (Phylloquinone)
microNutrients.description: An abundant dose of this critical fat-soluble factor, essential for managing natural blood coagulation cascades and anchoring bone calcium.

microNutrients.name: Sulforaphane (Glucoraphanin)
microNutrients.description: A legendary sulfur-rich compound unique to cruciferous vegetables that activates profound cellular detoxification and deep antioxidant defense.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B9 (Folate)
microNutrients.description: Crucial coenzyme necessary for continuous cellular division, proper DNA replication, and protecting vascular tissue equilibrium.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A rich mix of soluble and insoluble structural fibers that optimize digestive transit times and heavily feed beneficial gut flora.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An essential systemic electrolyte coordinating healthy fluid mechanics, neuromuscular impulses, and resting vascular tone.

healthBenefits: Advanced Cellular Detoxification: The rich presence of glucoraphanin converts into *sulforaphane* upon chewing or chopping, triggering profound liver detox pathways and fighting systemic free-radical decay.

Elite Vascular & Immune Defense: Delivering nearly 100% of your daily Vitamin C per 100g, it aggressively drives white blood cell production while working with Vitamin K1 to support vascular lining flexibility.

Skeletal Mineral Anchoring: High natural levels of Vitamin K1 efficiently coordinate osteocalcin activation, ensuring calcium routes smoothly out of blood vessels and locks tightly into the structural bone matrix.
Robust Glycemic Control: Complex structural fibers combined with slow-burning starches delay gastric empty rates, keeping post-meal blood sugar curves phenomenally stable.
precautions: Cruciferous Goitrogen Activity: Raw broccoli contains trace amounts of goitrogens—plant compounds that can theoretically compete with iodine absorption in the thyroid. For individuals with compromised thyroid health, lightly steaming completely neutralizes this effect.

Gastrointestinal Gas & Fermentation: Packed with dense, rigid cellulose fibers and a complex sugar called raffinose, raw broccoli can be tough to break down for sensitive stomachs, causing temporary bloating or lower abdominal gas. Cooked formats soften these structures significantly.

Calibrated Blood Thinner Synergy: Due to the high, rich volume of Vitamin K1—the master coordinator of the body's natural blood clotting mechanics—individuals taking prescription anticoagulants (like Warfarin) should maintain steady, highly consistent intake.

Thermal Enzyme Deactivation: Boiling broccoli inside excessive water for long periods kills *myrosinase*—the crucial enzyme required to unlock its highly therapeutic sulforaphane compound. Lightly steaming for 3 to 5 minutes is optimal for preserving its functional value.

carrot.name: Carrot
carrot.description:
Carrots (Daucus carota) are vibrant, biennial root vegetables cultivated globally for their crisp texture and nutrient density. Traditionally associated with a deep orange hue, they also grow in heritage varieties of purple, yellow, red, and white.
                            From a botanical perspective, carrots belong to the Apiaceae (parsley) family, sharing lineage with celery, parsnips, and fennel. While the sweet, taproot is the most commonly consumed part, the feathery green tops are also edible and rich in minerals. Carrots owe their signature orange color to highly concentrated carotenoid pigments, which serve as crucial precursors for essential vitamins in human metabolism.
carrot.macroIntro: Carrots are a low-calorie, high-moisture crop composed of approximately 88% water. They provide clean energy primarily through complex carbohydrates, with a negligible fat profile.
carrot.microIntro: Carrots are a premier dietary source of provitamin A and contain an array of synergistic micronutrients that support cellular integrity.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Provides low-glycemic basal energy to fuel daily metabolic processes.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Minimal; contains trace structural amino acids necessary for plant protein structures.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Negligible; mostly composed of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Split between naturally occurring simple sugars (sucrose, glucose) and structural complex carbohydrates.

macroNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
macroNutrients.description: Rich in soluble pectin and insoluble cellulose that optimize digestion and support gut microbiota.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A
microNutrients.description: Packed with beta-carotene and alpha-carotene, which the liver converts into retinol for advanced vision and night sight protection.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K1
microNutrients.description: Essential for synthesizing blood-coagulation proteins and supporting structural bone mineralization.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6
microNutrients.description: Serves as a vital coenzyme in cellular amino acid metabolism, energy release, and neurotransmitter production.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An essential intracellular electrolyte that regulates fluid balance, nerve signaling, and systemic blood pressure.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: A water-soluble antioxidant that strengthens endothelial defenses, drives collagen synthesis, and boosts immunity.

microNutrients.name: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
microNutrients.description: Crucial carotenoid antioxidants that accumulate in the macular region of the eye, filtering harmful blue light wavelengths.

healthBenefits: Advanced Vision Protection: The high concentration of beta-carotene is utilized by the retina to synthesize rhodopsin, a biological pigment necessary for low-light and night vision. Additionally, carrots contain lutein, an antioxidant that accumulates in the macular region of the eye, filtering out harmful blue light wavelengths and mitigating the risk of age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

Cardiovascular & Glycemic Regulation: The soluble fiber profile in carrots consists heavily of pectin, which binds bile acids in the intestinal lumen, prompting the liver to draw cholesterol from the bloodstream to synthesize more bile—effectively lowering circulating LDL cholesterol. Despite their sweet taste, carrots have a low glycemic index (GI ~16 to 32 depending on raw vs. cooked states), preventing rapid blood glucose spikes.

Digestive Tract Optimization: The insoluble fibers (cellulose and hemicellulose) add bulk to fecal matter and stimulate peristalsis, preventing constipation. Furthermore, these fibers act as prebiotics, feeding beneficial short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria in the large intestine, which fortifies the gut barrier function.

Endothelial and Immune Defense: Carotenoids and vitamin C act as potent free-radical scavengers, dampening systemic oxidative stress and protecting vascular endothelial cell walls. Vitamin A also regulates the differentiation and activation of T-cells and B-lymphocytes, reinforcing the body's primary immune response against pathogens.
precautions: Carotenemia: Excessive, chronic consumption of carrots can lead to carotenemia—a benign clinical condition where excess beta-carotene accumulates in the stratum corneum, causing a distinct yellowish-orange discoloration of the skin (most visible on the palms and soles). It is completely reversible by reducing intake.

Pesticide Residuals & Soil Hygiene: Because carrots are subterranean taproots, they directly absorb chemicals present in the soil. Thorough scrubbing or peeling is highly recommended for conventional carrots to eliminate pesticide residues and pathogens like Listeria or Toxoplasma gondii.

Oral Allergy Syndrome (OAS): Individuals allergic to birch pollen or mugwort may experience cross-reactivity when eating raw carrots due to structural similarities in plant proteins. Symptoms include localized itching or swelling of the lips, mouth, and throat. Cooking the carrots denatures these proteins, typically eliminating the reaction.

corn.name: Corn
corn.description: Corn is a vibrant, carbohydrate-rich vegetable and cereal grain. Highly regarded for its exceptional content of protective macular carotenoids like lutein and zeaxanthin, it provides a functional balance of dietary fibers and B-vitamins to sustain physical stamina and ocular health.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A moderate-energy starchy vegetable that provides sustained, reliable fuel for muscular work and cellular respiration.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains a notable amount of plant proteins for a vegetable, including zein, though it should be paired with legumes for a complete amino profile.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Naturally very low in fat, containing trace heart-healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids within the grain germ.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Primarily composed of complex starches and natural simple sugars, offering structured energy management to prevent rapid glucose spikes.

microNutrients.name: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
microNutrients.description: Phenomenal plant pigments that deposit directly into the macular region of the eye, filtering harmful blue light and guarding visual acuity.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamin)
microNutrients.description: An essential coenzyme involved in carbohydrate metabolic cascades, crucial for optimizing cognitive drive and nervous system communication.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B9 (Folate)
microNutrients.description: Vital for cellular division, nucleotide synthesis, and erythrocyte maturation, playing a protective role in cardiovascular tissue health.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: Mainly insoluble fibers that add mechanical volume to the stool matrix, accelerating intestinal transit and supporting digestive regularity.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Assists in enzymatic cellular stabilization, supporting muscular relaxation, bone health, and smooth cardiac electrical performance.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: Provides antioxidant assistance, neutralizing surface free radicals and supporting natural immune tissue integrity.

healthBenefits: Targeted Macular Defense: The high density of lutein and zeaxanthin acts as natural "internal sunglasses," shielding retinal cells against oxidative blue light exposure and slowing macular breakdown.
Sustained Glycemic Energy: Its complex starch matrix, balanced by dietary fibers, results in steady metabolic glucose release, preventing sudden insulin crashes when eaten in whole form.
Enhanced Bowel Motility: Rich in insoluble plant fiber, corn swells within the intestinal tract, physically sweeping the colon lining, boosting peristalsis, and preventing general sluggishness.
Neuro-Metabolic Support: Substantial amounts of Thiamin (B1) support cellular energy pathways, optimizing memory mechanics and structural peripheral nerve health.
precautions: Starchy Glycemic Load Factors: Corn contains significantly more carbohydrates than leafy or watery vegetables. Individuals managing Type 2 diabetes or tracking precise glycemic parameters should control serving volumes to avoid unexpected postprandial glucose shifts.

Insoluble Outer Husk Toughness: The clear cellulose shell wrapping each individual kernel is structurally un-digestible by human stomach acid. Improperly chewed corn can pass entirely intact, causing gas, mild cramps, or bloating in sensitive digestive tracts.

Hidden Syrups & Ultra-Processed Additives: While whole sweet corn is highly therapeutic, refined commercial corn offshoots—such as High-Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS) or processed corn starch—lack all fibers and minerals, severely aggravating metabolic liver pathways.

Fungal Mycotoxin Contamination: If stored in poorly ventilated, high-humidity corporate grain silos, corn crops can easily develop mold strains producing aflatoxins. Always consume freshly cooked or properly sealed, verified retail products.

cottage-cheese.name: Cottage Cheese
cottage-cheese.description: Cottage cheese is a fresh, curd-style dairy product celebrated globally by athletes and nutritionists. It is exceptionally rich in premium protein, remarkably low in baseline calories, and serves as an elite resource for slow-digesting amino acids.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Low-calorie energy base, making it an exceptional option for weight management and lean muscle retention.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Packed with slow-digesting casein protein, which delivers a steady, multi-hour release of essential amino acids to muscles.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Contains a balance of fatty acids, including healthy lipids that aid in the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins without overloading calories.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Comes mostly from naturally occurring lactose. It has a very low glycemic impact, preventing sudden blood sugar spikes.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: The primary structural mineral required for developing and preserving high bone density and optimizing dental health.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: Crucial for the neurological system, sound brain signaling, and the continuous synthesis of healthy red blood cells.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus
microNutrients.description: Works synchronously with calcium to rebuild bone matrices, while supporting cellular ATP energy storage.

microNutrients.name: Selenium
microNutrients.description: An essential trace mineral that acts as an antioxidant defense catalyst and regulates thyroid hormone production.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
microNutrients.description: A key coenzyme that enables metabolic breakdown of proteins, fats, and carbs into usable cellular energy.

microNutrients.name: Sodium
microNutrients.description: An extracellular electrolyte used during commercial curd styling. It regulates physical fluid balancing and cellular pump mechanisms.

healthBenefits: Sustained Muscle Recovery: The dominant protein group here is casein (~80%). Because it clots in the stomach, it digests slowly, providing a sustained anti-catabolic flow of amino acids, making it perfect for an evening or before-bed snack.
Satiety & Weight Loss Architecture: Thanks to its high protein density, it triggers fullness hormones like peptide YY, suppressing hunger cues while keeping overall caloric intake low.
Skeletal System Integrity: High concentrations of calcium and phosphorus directly nourish bone matrices and teeth, reducing risks associated with early bone density decline.
Metabolic Boost: Packed with B-complex vitamins that act as essential cellular catalysts, converting consumed food matrices into clean metabolic energy.
precautions: Lactose Intolerance Profile: Being a fresh, unaged cheese, it retains natural milk sugars. Individuals with severe lactose intolerance might experience gastrointestinal distress and should seek out lactose-free variants.

Elevated Sodium Content: Commercial manufacturing relies on sodium to process curd texture and longevity. If you are watching your blood pressure or managing structural kidney load, track the sodium content carefully or opt for low-sodium brands.
Dairy Allergies: Cottage cheese contains intact whey and casein structures. This makes it unsafe for individuals with a confirmed, IgE-mediated milk allergy.
Storage and Freshness: Fresh cheeses have high moisture contents and spoil rapidly. Always keep tightly sealed at or below 4°C (40°F) and consume within a few days of opening.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.description: Eggs are often called "nature's multivitamin" for a good reason. They are one of the most nutritionally dense, complete whole foods available, packed with high-quality protein, healthy fats, and a wide array of essential vitamins and minerals.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Energy provided by the food to fuel your body's daily metabolic processes and physical activities.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: High-quality, bioavailable protein containing all nine essential amino acids. Essential for muscle repair, cellular construction, and immune function.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Includes healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats, alongside essential fatty acids, vital for hormone production and absorbing fat-soluble vitamins.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Extremely low in carbs, making eggs an excellent choice for stabilizing blood sugar and supporting low-glycemic dietary targets.

microNutrients.name: Choline
microNutrients.description: Critical for brain development, memory, and cellular structural integrity. One egg provides roughly 25-30% of your daily requirement.

healthBenefits: Promotes Muscle Maintenance & Recovery: The highly bioavailable protein in eggs makes them an excellent food for tissue repair and building lean muscle mass.
Supports Brain Health: The high concentration of choline is used by the brain to synthesize acetylcholine, a neurotransmitter critical for memory, mood, and cognitive function.

Improves Heart Health Architecture: While eggs do contain dietary cholesterol, extensive research shows that for about 70% of the population, dietary cholesterol does not significantly raise blood cholesterol. In fact, egg consumption typically improves the lipid profile by raising "good" HDL cholesterol and changing the texture of "bad" LDL to large, less harmful particles.
Aids Weight Management: High protein foods increase satiety (the feeling of fullness) and regulate appetite hormones, which can naturally reduce subsequent calorie intake throughout the day.
Protects Vision: The antioxidants lutein and zeaxanthin accumulate in the retina, drastically lowering the risk of age-related cataracts and macular health decline.
eggs.precautionsIntro: The Salmonella Risk: Raw or undercooked eggs can carry Salmonella enteritidis, a bacteria that causes food poisoning. Always cook eggs until the yolks and whites are firm, or use pasteurized eggs for recipes requiring raw components (like homemade mayo or tiramisu).
precautions: Egg Allergies: Egg allergy is one of the most common food allergies, especially in children. Symptoms can range from mild hives to severe anaphylaxis. Fortunately, many children outgrow it by adolescence.

Hyper-Responders to Cholesterol: About 30% of people are "hyper-responders," meaning dietary cholesterol significantly impacts their blood levels. If you have a genetic predisposition to high cholesterol, familial hypercholesterolemia, or existing type 2 diabetes, it is wise to monitor your overall egg intake and consult a medical professional.

Proper Storage: Eggs should be stored in their original carton in the main body of the refrigerator (at or below 4°C / 40°F) rather than the refrigerator door, where temperature fluctuations are highest.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Smoothness & Architecture: The heavy input of marine EPA and DHA lowers blood triglycerides, optimizes arterial elasticity, reduces resting blood pressure, and helps stabilize heart rhythms.

Advanced Cognitive Optimization: Since DHA is a primary structural lipid component of the human brain cortex, consistent consumption preserves optimal neuro-signaling, boosts memory parameters, and mitigates age-related cognitive decline.

Powerful Systemic Anti-Inflammation: Marine omega-3 fats directly compete with inflammatory pathways, drastically decreasing the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and protecting metabolic tissues.
Skeletal & Immune Reinforcement: Exceptional natural concentrations of active Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) maximize intestinal calcium absorption, consolidating skeletal bone density matrices.
precautions: Mercury & Heavy Metal Bioaccumulation: Large predatory fish species (like swordfish, king mackerel, and large tuna) can accumulate mercury in their muscle tissue over time. For frequent eating, choose smaller species like salmon, sardines, or trout.

Environmental Pollutant Thresholds: Wild-caught fish from heavily industrialized water bodies may contain trace persistent organic pollutants (POPs) or PCBs. Sourcing your seafood from certified, environmentally sustainable fisheries is highly advised.

Fish and Seafood Allergies: Fish allergy is highly prevalent and typically persists throughout adulthood, carrying a high risk of triggering severe, immediate anaphylactic reactions in sensitive individuals.

Perishability & Histamine Toxicity: If fatty fish is stored incorrectly or sits too long before freezing, the rapid bacterial breakdown of histidine can cause high histamine accumulation, leading to scombroid food poisoning.

healthBenefits: Elite Digestive Enhancement: Kiwi naturally produces *actinidin*, a highly functional protease enzyme that breaks down dense dietary proteins (like red meats or dairy), drastically speeding up gastric emptying and easing bloating.
Unrivaled Immune Fortification: Supplying over 100% of your daily Vitamin C value per 100g, kiwi drives rapid neutrophil leukocyte activity, helping guard systemic tissues from common pathogens.

Intestinal Motility & Regularity: The high water-binding capacity of kiwi's unique soluble and insoluble fibers softens the stool matrix and significantly optimizes bowel movement consistency without bloating.
Endothelial Vasodilation: The healthy presence of potassium and organic antioxidants aids in inhibiting blood platelet aggregation, helping manage lipid health and keeping blood pressure balanced.
precautions: High Allergenic Potential: Kiwi is a well-documented source of cross-reactive food allergens, primarily due to actinidin. Symptoms of a kiwi allergy include oral allergy syndrome (itching or tingling in the mouth and throat), hives, and in severe cases, anaphylaxis.

The Gelatin Cooking Conflict: Because actinidin aggressively breaks down protein molecules, using fresh raw kiwi in recipes containing gelatin or milk proteins will destroy the structure, preventing jello from setting or making dairy taste bitter.

Oral Mucosal Soreness: Consuming multiple raw kiwis at once can cause a temporary stinging or burning sensation on the tongue and inner cheeks. This is a harmless physical reaction caused by actinidin enzymes and microscopic needle-like calcium oxalate crystals (raphides) physically irritating the soft tissues.

Moderate Oxalate Content: Kiwi contains measurable amounts of natural organic oxalates. Individuals with a historical predisposition to calcium-oxalate kidney stone formations should regulate excessive intake.

healthBenefits: Immune System Architecture: Mushrooms contain complex polysaccharides called beta-glucans. These molecules act as natural immunomodulators, gently binding to immune cells to optimize host defense activities.
Cellular Antioxidant Defense: The robust concentration of selenium helps generate crucial glutathione peroxidase enzymes, shielding cellular membranes from everyday oxidative destruction.

Cardiovascular Health Support: Naturally rich in potassium and completely clear of sodium or cholesterol, mushrooms facilitate relaxed vascular tension and aid in proper systemic blood pressure control.
Satiety with Minimal Calories: Their dense structural matrix provides substantial dietary weight and a satisfying savory "umami" experience, keeping you full while incurring very low caloric costs.
precautions: Chitin Digestive Resistance: Raw mushroom cell walls are built from chitin—a tough, rigid polymer. To avoid digestive strain, cramping, or bloating, mushrooms should always be cooked to break down this matrix.

Foraging and Wild Toxicity Risk: Never consume wild mushrooms unless they have been verified with absolute professional certainty. Toxic varieties can mimic edible species perfectly and cause fatal organ damage. Commercial store-bought options are completely safe.

Porous Heavy Metal Absorption: Fungi act like natural sponges, easily drawing pollutants or heavy metals from contaminated surrounding soil. Always purchase your mushrooms from trusted, quality-controlled cultivation vendors.

Perishability and Mold Growth: Due to high baseline moisture levels, fresh mushrooms spoil quickly and can harbor toxic molds if stored incorrectly. Keep them in breathable paper bags in the fridge and discard if they become slimy.

healthBenefits: Ophthalmological Protection: High beta-carotene and zeaxanthin content protect the retina from damage caused by light exposure.
Cardio-metabolic Support: Adenosine and potassium work synergistically to improve coronary blood flow and control blood pressure.
Skin Regeneration: High levels of vitamin C and antioxidants stimulate epithelial tissue renewal and improve skin turgor.
Detoxification and Hydration: Possesses a mild diuretic effect, promoting the cleansing of urinary tracts and maintaining overall fluid levels in the body.
melon.precautionsIntro: Melon is an active enzymatic product that requires careful attention regarding how it is consumed:
precautions: GI Fermentation: Consuming melon immediately after a heavy protein or fatty meal often leads to excessive fermentation, causing bloating and heaviness. It is recommended to consume it as a separate meal.
Glycemic Risk: Contains easily digestible sugars; individuals with diabetes should strictly dose consumption to avoid glycemic spikes.
Nitrate Load: Like other gourd crops, melons are prone to accumulating nitrogen fertilizers in the rind. It is necessary to clean the pulp thoroughly, avoiding the area near the rind.
Individual Sensitivity: High sugar content can exacerbate conditions associated with Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth (SIBO).

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.description: Cucumber is a highly hydrating vegetable matrix possessing low energy density and a high concentration of electrolytes. It serves as a fundamental tool for maintaining systemic water balance and detoxifying the body, providing a supply of phytochemical compounds (cucurbitacins) that possess anti-inflammatory and protective potential.
cucumber.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100g, raw product with peel)
cucumber.macroIntro: The macronutrient composition of cucumber is almost entirely focused on supporting hydration, making it an indispensable component of metabolic weight loss protocols.
cucumber.microIntro: The product is a unique source of organic silica and specific polyphenols that act synergistically on the integrity of connective tissue and the antioxidant defense of cells.

healthBenefits: Hydration Optimization: Cucumber's structured water has high bioavailability, contributing to the efficient excretion of metabolic waste products.
Connective Tissue Support: High silica content strengthens structural proteins, promoting skin elasticity and the durability of bone structures.
Glycemic Profile Regulation: Due to its low glycemic index and fiber content, cucumber does not trigger an insulin response.
Anti-inflammatory Activity: Cucurbitacins and flavonoids systemically reduce markers of inflammation, protecting cells from premature aging.
cucumber.precautionsIntro: Cucumber is considered a safe product; however, to prevent side effects, consumption specifics should be considered:
precautions: Nitrate Profile: Early-season and greenhouse cucumbers are prone to nitrate accumulation, especially in the peel and near the stem. Peeling is recommended if the origin is uncertain.
Bloating in IBS: In individuals with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) or flatulence, consuming raw cucumbers may provoke discomfort due to the high fiber content and specific sugars.
Anti-nutrient Components: The presence of cucurbitacins in some varieties may impart bitterness and, in excess, cause mild gastric mucosal irritation.
Compatibility: Due to enzymatic activity, cucumbers are not always recommended to be mixed with dairy products, as this may provoke digestive disturbances in individuals with sensitive GI tracts.

kefir.name: Kefir
kefir.description: Kefir is a highly effective fermented probiotic matrix obtained by fermenting milk with kefir grains. It represents a complex symbiosis of beneficial bacteria and yeasts, possessing a marked modulating effect on the intestinal microbiota and the body's systemic immune reactivity.
kefir.macroIntro: The macronutrient profile of kefir is balanced to provide the body with easily digestible proteins and a moderate amount of dairy fats, which contributes to high-quality tissue regeneration.
kefir.microIntro: Kefir is a unique carrier of metabolically active compounds, B-vitamins, and organic acids, working synergistically to support the body's internal environment.

microNutrients.description: Participates in oxidation-reduction reaction processes and vision maintenance.

microNutrients.name: Organic Acids
microNutrients.description: Lactic and acetic acids, creating an optimal pH environment in the gut.

healthBenefits: Microbiome Correction: Kefir is one of the most powerful natural sources of probiotics that restore the diversity of intestinal flora.
Immune Modulation: Through its impact on the GALT system (gut-associated lymphoid tissue), systematic consumption of kefir increases the body's overall resistance.
GI Optimization: Organic acids and enzymes contribute to efficient food digestion and regular bowel motility.
Metabolic Improvement: Regular consumption contributes to improving the cholesterol profile and stabilizing blood sugar levels.
kefir.precautionsIntro: Kefir is a biologically active product, so it is important to consider individual characteristics when including it in the diet:
precautions: Lactose Intolerance: Despite partial lactose breakdown, people with severe lactase deficiency may experience symptoms of indigestion.
Acidity: High organic acid content may cause discomfort in individuals with hyperacidic gastritis or peptic ulcers in the acute stage.
Alcohol Content: Natural kefir contains trace amounts of ethanol (a result of yeast fermentation). This amount is minimal, but should be considered if strictly abstaining.
Product Freshness: Kefir has different effects on the GI tract depending on storage time: fresh (one-day) has a mild laxative effect, while 'old' (three-day) has a constipating effect.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.description: Cheese is a highly concentrated protein-lipid matrix obtained through the fermentation and coagulation of milk protein. It is a nutritionally dense product that serves as a rich source of bioavailable calcium, complete animal protein, and fat-soluble vitamins, providing structural support for the skeletal system and metabolic processes.
cheese.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100g, average values for semi-hard varieties)
cheese.macroIntro: Cheese is characterized by high energy density and an optimal ratio of macronutrients, making it a strategic product for maintaining muscle tone and energy balance.
cheese.microIntro: The product is a unique storehouse of essential nutrients, including vitamins A, D, and B12, and mineral elements that work synergistically to maintain physiological homeostasis.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus

microNutrients.name: Zinc

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K2

healthBenefits: Skeletal Support: The unique combination of calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin K2 provides fundamental strength to bone structures.
Protein Synthesis: The high concentration of casein makes cheese an effective product for maintaining muscle mass and long-term metabolic satiety.
Oral Health: Regular cheese consumption helps increase the oral cavity's pH, reducing tooth enamel demineralization.
Neuroendocrine Stability: Cheese fats and amino acids contribute to maintaining hormonal balance and cognitive functions.
cheese.precautionsIntro: Cheese is a highly active product, so it should be included in the diet considering the following aspects:
precautions: Sodium Content: Hard and aged varieties often contain high doses of salt, which requires monitoring in cases of arterial hypertension or kidney disease.
Saturated Fats: The high content of saturated fatty acids requires portion limitation for individuals with dyslipidemia and a tendency toward cardiovascular pathologies.
Amines and Histamine: Aged cheeses contain tyramine and other biogenic amines that may provoke headaches in sensitive individuals.
Individual Intolerance: Despite the low lactose content, allergy to dairy proteins (casein) is a direct contraindication for consuming most types of cheese.

lemon.name: Lemon
lemon.description: Lemon is a highly concentrated biochemical agent belonging to the Rutaceae family. It is valued for its unique content of citric acid, high doses of ascorbic acid, and a wide spectrum of phytonutrients (flavonoids), which provide powerful antioxidant protection and optimization of metabolic processes in the body.
lemon.macroIntro: Lemon is characterized by extremely low caloric content and an almost total absence of fat and protein, making it a tool for flavor and nutritional modulation of dishes without significantly changing their energy density.
lemon.microIntro: The product is a complex storehouse of vitamins and organic compounds, playing a critical role in maintaining immune status and systemic detoxification.

microNutrients.description: An organic acid that promotes improved digestion and helps prevent kidney stone formation.

microNutrients.name: Flavonoids
microNutrients.description: Hesperidin and eriocitrin—compounds protecting cells from oxidative damage.

microNutrients.name: Potassium

microNutrients.name: Folate (B9)

healthBenefits: Immune Stimulation: High concentration of Vitamin C activates the phagocytic activity of immune system cells.
Cardiovascular Support: Flavonoids and potassium contribute to reducing systemic vascular inflammation and normalizing blood pressure.
Renal Prophylaxis: Citric acid increases urinary citrate levels, which inhibits the crystallization of oxalate stones.
Metabolic Activation: Consuming lemon water promotes the stimulation of digestive enzyme secretion.
lemon.precautionsIntro: Despite the benefits, the high acidity of lemon requires caution in the following conditions:
precautions: GERD: High acidity may provoke heartburn and esophageal mucosal irritation in individuals with GERD.
Enamel Erosion: Direct contact of lemon juice with teeth demineralizes the enamel. Using a straw or rinsing the mouth with water is recommended.
Ulcerative Lesions: In cases of gastritis or stomach ulcer exacerbation, lemon juice consumption is strictly not recommended due to the risk of mucosal damage.
Allergic Reactions: Citrus fruits are known allergens. Individuals with hypersensitivity should exercise caution when introducing them for the first time.

peaches.name: Peaches
peaches.description: The peach is a highly functional fruit, representing a concentrated matrix of organic acids, soluble fibers, and carotenoid pigments. It is an effective metabolic modulator that supports the health of epithelial tissues, immune function, and the body's optimal antioxidant balance.
peaches.macroIntro: The macronutrient composition of the peach is characterized by moderate energy density and high sugar availability, ensuring the rapid restoration of glycogen stores during physical activity.
peaches.microIntro: Peaches are a unique source of polyphenolic compounds that work synergistically to reduce systemic inflammation and protect cellular structures from oxidative damage.

healthBenefits: Dermatological Support: The high concentration of vitamins and antioxidants contributes to improved skin turgor and protection against UV-induced damage.
Cardioprotection: Regular consumption of peaches contributes to the normalization of blood lipid profiles and the reduction of systemic inflammation.
Digestive Modulation: Soluble fibers promote smooth food transit and prevent digestive disturbances.
Antioxidant Status: Phenolic compounds and carotenoids neutralize free radicals, slowing down cellular aging processes.
peaches.precautionsIntro: Peaches are a safe product, but their consumption should take into account physiological characteristics:
precautions: Allergic Reactions: Due to the presence of specific lipid-transfer proteins (LTP), peaches can cause food allergies, especially in individuals with pollinosis (pollen allergy).
Glycemic Profile: Although the fruit has a moderate glycemic index, individuals with diabetes should limit the consumption of very sweet varieties.
Dyspepsia: In people with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) or fructose intolerance, consuming large amounts of peaches can provoke fermentation and gas.
Nitrate Load: Like other fruits, peaches can accumulate fertilizers if agricultural protocols are violated, so thorough washing of the fruits is recommended.

dill.name: Dill
dill.description: Dill is a biologically active phytomatrix possessing pronounced antispasmodic, carminative, and antibacterial potential. It is a concentrate of essential oils (notably carvone and limonene), which modulate digestive tract functions and support the systemic antioxidant status of the organism.
dill.macroIntro: Dill is a low-calorie product with an extremely low density of macronutrients, making it a valuable functional addition to the diet without significantly altering energy balance.
dill.microIntro: The product is a unique source of phytonutrients and trace elements working synergistically to normalize metabolism and support immune system health.

healthBenefits: Digestive Modulation: Dill effectively relaxes the smooth muscles of the intestines, eliminating spasms, bloating, and flatulence.
Antimicrobial Activity: The phytoncides contained in the plant suppress pathogenic flora, contributing to the improvement of the intestinal environment.
Metabolic Support: High content of vitamins and minerals strengthens the body's protective barrier and contributes to general recovery.
Cardiovascular Regulation: Dill flavonoids contribute to blood pressure stabilization and the reduction of systemic inflammation.
dill.precautionsIntro: Dill is safe when used in culinary doses, but requires consideration of some nuances:
precautions: Photosensitivity: When taking concentrated dill extracts, increased skin sensitivity to ultraviolet light (photosensitization) is possible.
Hypotension: Excessive consumption of dill can lead to an excessive decrease in blood pressure, which is important for individuals prone to hypotension.
Allergic Reactions: In individuals sensitive to plants of the Apiaceae family, dill consumption may provoke allergic reactions.
Pregnancy: In pharmacological doses, dill extracts are not recommended during pregnancy due to potential effects on uterine tone.

parsley.name: Parsley
parsley.description: Parsley is a nutritionally dense phytomatrix possessing powerful diuretic and anti-inflammatory potential. It serves as a unique source of vitamins C, K, and specific flavonoids (apigenin), which exert a protective effect on the vascular wall and support the body's antioxidant homeostasis.
parsley.macroIntro: Parsley is characterized by low energy density with a significant content of bioactive compounds, making it an ideal component for the functional enrichment of any diet.
parsley.microIntro: The plant is a biochemical concentrate of essential nutrients that contribute to the detoxification of the body and the improvement of the metabolic profile.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Protection: Apigenin and folic acid contribute to lowering homocysteine levels and improving arterial elasticity.
Diuretic Effect: Myristicin and apiol contained in parsley oil stimulate kidney function, facilitating the excretion of excess fluid.
Bone Mineralization: An extremely high concentration of Vitamin K ensures correct calcium fixation in bone tissue.
Antioxidant Support: High levels of vitamins C and A systemically suppress free radical activity.
parsley.precautionsIntro: Parsley is a product with pronounced biological activity, so the following should be considered:
precautions: Pregnancy: In concentrated forms (essential oils), parsley may stimulate uterine contractions, so it should be avoided in therapeutic doses.
Kidney Disease: Due to high oxalate content, regular consumption of very large doses of greens requires caution if prone to kidney stones.
Interaction with Anticoagulants: High levels of Vitamin K may reduce the effectiveness of blood-thinning medications (e.g., warfarin).
Allergy: Individual hypersensitivity to plants of the Apiaceae family is possible.

apricot.description: The apricot is a functional fruit that serves as a concentrated source of carotenoids and potassium. It is an effective metabolic agent that promotes optimization of the cardiovascular system, improves tissue regeneration, and supports the body's antioxidant homeostasis.

Digestive Optimization: Fiber improves peristalsis, preventing constipation and supporting gut microbiota.
Tissue Regeneration: The combination of vitamins A, C, and E accelerates the healing of epithelial structures.
apricot.precautionsIntro: Apricots are beneficial, but their consumption has physiological limitations:
precautions: Sugar Content: In dried form, sugar concentration is extremely high, requiring monitoring in cases of diabetes.
Acidity: Large quantities of consumed fresh apricots can provoke a laxative effect and discomfort in people with sensitive GI tracts.
Pits: The kernels of the pits contain amygdalin, which releases cyanide during metabolism. Consuming large amounts of kernels is dangerous.
Allergy: Individual intolerance is possible, especially in individuals sensitive to birch pollen or other stone fruits.

whole-wheat-bread.name: Whole Wheat Bread
whole-wheat-bread.description: Whole wheat bread is a high-energy matrix of complex carbohydrates obtained from flour containing all parts of the grain (bran, endosperm, and germ). It is a fundamental source of slowly released glucose, dietary fiber, and a wide spectrum of micronutrients necessary for maintaining metabolic stability and GI tract health.
whole-wheat-bread.macroIntro: The macronutrient profile of the product is balanced to provide prolonged satiety, preventing sharp insulin spikes in the systemic bloodstream.
whole-wheat-bread.microIntro: The bread serves as a carrier for key B-vitamins and minerals that play a critical role in nervous system functioning and energy metabolism.

Intestinal Support: Fiber stimulates peristalsis and creates an environment for the proliferation of beneficial microflora.
Cardiovascular Support: Regular consumption of whole grains is associated with a lower risk of hypertension and CHD.
Satiety and Weight Control: High fiber content ensures rapid satiety, helping to control the volume of consumed calories.
whole-wheat-bread.precautionsIntro: Despite its high nutritional value, whole wheat bread requires consideration of some aspects:
precautions: Gluten Sensitivity: For individuals with celiac disease or gluten intolerance, consumption of this product is strictly contraindicated.
Anti-nutrients: Whole grains contain phytic acid, which can reduce the bioavailability of certain minerals (zinc, calcium) if consumed in excess.
GI Irritation: In individuals with acute gastritis or irritable bowel syndrome, rough fibers can cause mechanical irritation of the mucosa.
Raw Material Quality: It is important to choose products made from quality grain, as bran can accumulate pesticides if stored improperly.

whole-grain-pasta.name: Whole Grain Pasta
whole-grain-pasta.description: Whole grain pasta is a nutritionally enriched form of a carbohydrate matrix produced from whole wheat flour, which retains all grain layers: bran, endosperm, and germ. Appetite Control: Prolonged digestion and satiety facilitate the control of energy balance and body weight.
whole-grain-pasta.precautionsIntro: Whole grain pasta is a safe product but has limitations:

Gastroenterological Conditions: During acute gastritis or peptic ulcer disease, coarse fiber may cause mechanical irritation of the mucosa.
Mineral Bioavailability: Phytic acid contained in bran may partially block the absorption of zinc and iron if consumed in excess.
Individual Intolerance: In individuals with heightened sensitivity to wheat components, uncomfortable GI reactions are possible.

beetroot.name: Beetroot
beetroot.description: Beetroot is a highly functional root vegetable possessing a unique profile of bioactive compounds, including betalains (plant pigments) and nitrates. sour-cream.description: Sour cream is a fermented milk product obtained by fermenting cream with lactic acid bacteria. It is valued for its content of probiotics, fat-soluble vitamins, and calcium, which are necessary for bone tissue and intestinal microflora.
sour-cream.macroIntro: A product with high energy density, consisting mainly of milk fats.
sour-cream.microIntro: It is a source of calcium and B vitamins.

butter.name: Butter
butter.description: Butter is concentrated milk fat obtained by churning cream. It is an important source of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K2) and conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), which has potential anti-carcinogenic properties.
butter.macroIntro: A product with maximum energy density, consisting almost entirely of lipids.
butter.microIntro: Contains a unique profile of fat-soluble micronutrients.

butter.precautionsIntro: Due to its high energy density and fat composition, moderation is recommended:

Individual Intolerance: Contraindicated for those with a dairy protein (casein) allergy or lactose intolerance (depending on purity).
